## 3. Inaccessible photons are included in the guarantee

The vacuum branch above is a term in the proof; the protocol does not demand a measurement of the lost field.

Here the source has an unusually useful property:

\[
L_S^\dagger L_S=\gamma I.
\]

Every source photon trajectory has a scalar probability factor multiplying a product of unitaries. Hence its total emitted photon number is exactly

\[
N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\mu),
\]

independently of the unknown input and its reference. Uniform collection loss gives independent counts

\[
N_{\rm collected}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\eta\mu),
\qquad
N_{\rm lost}\sim\operatorname{Pois}((1-\eta)\mu).
\]

The downstream loss and cold receivers preserve photon number plus retained receiver excitations.

Let the output detector have efficiency \(\zeta\), with no-click effect

\[
(1-\zeta)^{\hat N_{\rm out}}.
\]

It needs only a no-click flag over the complete window, not number resolution or precise arrival times. Setting \(\zeta=0\) recovers the protocol without a detector.

Write \(\lambda=\eta\mu\). If the receivers retain \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\) excitations after \(n\) collected photons, exactly \(n-k\) photons remain in the outgoing field. The filter’s probability weights are

\[
w_0=u^4,\qquad w_1=u^2,\qquad w_2=1.
\]

Define

\[
f_k=
e^{-\lambda}
\sum_{n=k}^{\infty}
(1-\zeta)^{n-k}\frac{\lambda^n}{n!}.
\]

After decoding and discarding the auxiliary receiver, the complete successful instrument has the exact form

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_{\checkmark}
=p_0\,\mathrm{id}+\mathcal E,
\qquad
\mathcal E\ \text{completely positive},
}
\]

with

\[
\boxed{
\|\mathcal E\|_\diamond\le
b:=
\sum_{k=0}^{2}w_k
\left[
f_k-e^{-\mu}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}
\right].
}
\]

The subtracted term removes the event containing exactly \(k\) collected photons and no lost photons, which cannot contribute an erroneous residual-field branch when \(k\) excitations are retained. The remaining terms include collection loss, receiver re-emission and missed detector clicks. Because \(F^\dagger F\) is excitation-number diagonal, coherences between photon-number sectors do not invalidate this probability bound.

\[
p(\rho)\ge p_0,
\]

\frac12\left\|
\frac{(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\mathcal M_{\checkmark})(\rho_{AS})}
{p(\rho)}
